mainTopic: Is exactly half like a majority? Then, which lines of the משנה about cutting most of a סימן refer to חולין and which to קדשים.
overview: The amud opens by testing whether exactly half (מחצה על מחצה) counts like a majority (רוב) in שחיטה. A ברייתא about pausing after cutting half the windpipe is answered by saying it is about a bird. A second ברייתא, about a windpipe already half damaged, gets רבא's answer that טרפה needs a majority you can see. אביי knocks this down with a כל דכן. So the גמרא concludes that for שחיטה everyone agrees half is not a majority, and the argument of רב and רב כהנא was really about a nation half טמא at פסח time. Next the גמרא asks why the משנה repeats that most of a סימן is enough. רב הושעיא answers that one line is about חולין and one is about קדשים, and the גמרא explains why each is needed. רב כהנא, רב שימי בר אשי, רב פפא and רב אשי each prove that the first line is about חולין and the later line is about קדשים. ריש לקיש agrees, explaining that the later line teaches the יום כיפור תמיד is valid even if the cut was not finished. The גמרא then starts examining his words, a discussion that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A ברייתא about pausing after cutting half seems to contradict רב
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says that if someone cut half the windpipe, paused, and then finished, the שחיטה is kosher. If half counts as most, the animal should already have become a טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: ...[if he cut half the windpipe and paused] for the time it takes to slaughter another animal, and then finished it, his slaughter is valid. But if you say exactly half is like a majority, it already became a טרפה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting a ברייתא and uses it to challenge רב's rule that exactly half counts as most.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A windpipe that is cut through most of the way makes an animal a טרפה. If half counts as most, then once he cut half and stopped, the animal was a טרפה before the שחיטה was finished. Yet the ברייתא calls the שחיטה kosher, which seems to prove that half is not like most.

keyTerms.meaning: Exactly half-and-half is treated like a majority
The amount of time it takes to slaughter another animal
It became a טרפה (an animal that cannot live and is not kosher)

phrases.english: for the time of another slaughter, and then completed it,
his slaughter is valid.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אָמְרַתְּ מֶחֱצָה עַל מֶחֱצָה כְּרוֹב,
phrases.english: But if you say half-and-half is like a majority,
it became a tereifa!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי אָמְרַתְּ מֶחֱצָה עַל מֶחֱצָה כְּרוֹב, אִיטָּרְפָא לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a תא שמע challenge against רב that began before this section.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's rule that מחצה על מחצה כרוב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If half counts as most, cutting half the windpipe would make the animal a טרפה during the pause, yet the ברייתא rules the שחיטה kosher.

steps.title: The ברייתא is about a bird, so it works either way
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is talking about a bird, where only one סימן is needed. Whether half counts as most or not, the שחיטה is fine.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you think this is about an animal? No, it is about a bird! Either way: if half is like most, he already did the majority. If half is not like most, he did nothing at all.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב by saying the ברייתא is talking about a bird (עוף), not an animal (בהמה).
steps.deeperAnalysis: A bird needs only one סימן cut, and most of it is enough. If half counts as most, the שחיטה was already finished when he cut half, so the pause does not matter. If half does not count as most, he never made it a טרפה. Either way the ruling of 'kosher' fits, so the ברייתא proves nothing against רב.

keyTerms.meaning: A domesticated animal, which needs two סימנים cut
A bird, which needs only one סימן cut
Whichever way you look at it, the result is the same
He did nothing at all (nothing that counts)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the bird answer means רב is proven right. It only shows that this ברייתא fits both opinions, so it cannot be used against רב.

phrases.english: Do you think it is about an animal?
No, it is about a bird!
Whichever way you look at it:
if half-and-half is like a majority,
he has already done the majority,

phrases.aramaic: אִי מֶחֱצָה עַל מֶחֱצָה אֵינוֹ כְּרוֹב –
phrases.english: if half-and-half is not like a majority,
he did nothing at all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 1 by changing the case to a bird.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Recasting the case (אוקימתא): the ברייתא is about a bird
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא was understood as talking about an animal, where cutting half the windpipe would make it a טרפה.
steps.terutzMaskana: In a bird, the ruling is kosher whether or not half counts as most, so the ברייתא does not argue with רב.

steps.title: A second ברייתא about a windpipe that was already half damaged
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא says that if half the windpipe was already damaged, and the שוחט cut a tiny bit more and finished, the שחיטה is kosher. If half counts as most, the animal was already a טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: if half the windpipe was damaged, and he added any amount to it and finished, his slaughter is valid. But if you say half is like most, it is a טרפה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא to challenge רב's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the damage of half the windpipe happened before the שחיטה. If half counts as most, the animal was a טרפה before he even started, so the שחיטה should not help. The bird answer does not work here, because the problem is the old damage, not the pause.

keyTerms.meaning: The windpipe (trachea), one of the two סימנים
Damaged, having a cut or hole
Any amount, even a tiny bit
An animal with a fatal defect, which is forbidden to eat even after שחיטה

phrases.english: Come and hear:
If half the windpipe was damaged,
and he added any amount to it and completed it,
his slaughter is valid.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אָמְרַתְּ מֶחֱצָה עַל מֶחֱצָה כְּרוֹב –
phrases.english: And if you say half-and-half is like a majority,
it is a tereifa!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: הֲרֵי שֶׁהָיָה חֲצִי קָנֶה פָּגוּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first challenge was answered, the גמרא tries a new ברייתא against רב.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's rule that מחצה על מחצה כרוב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If half counts as most, a windpipe already damaged by half would have made the animal a טרפה before the שחיטה, yet the ברייתא calls it kosher.

steps.title: רבא: for טרפה, the majority must be visible
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that טרפה has its own rule: it needs a majority you can see with your eyes. Exactly half does not look like most, so the animal is not a טרפה. For שחיטה, half still counts as most.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: the law of טרפה is different, because there we need a majority that can be seen by the eyes.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends רב by saying the rule 'half is like most' applies to שחיטה, but not to טרפה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For an animal to become a טרפה, the damage must clearly look like most of the windpipe. Exactly half does not look that way, so the old damage did not make it a טרפה. This leaves רב's rule in place for שחיטה, while טרפה is a separate case with its own measure.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different
With regard to (a specific area of law)
A majority that is visible to the eyes

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא, 'half is like most' works for שחיטה. But for טרפה you need a majority that clearly looks like most, and exactly half does not.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the same measure (half vs. most) can be judged differently in different areas of הלכה: by strict count for שחיטה, and by how it looks for טרפה.

phrases.english: Rava said:
It is different with regard to tereifa,
since we require a majority visible to the eyes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 3 by separating the rule for טרפה from the rule for שחיטה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the areas of law (שאני): טרפה versus שחיטה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If half counts as most for שחיטה, it should also count as most for טרפה.
steps.terutzMaskana: טרפה requires a visible majority, so exactly half does not make the animal a טרפה. For שחיטה, half still counts as most.

steps.title: אביי argues that slaughter should need a visible majority even more than a טרפה
steps.stepSummary: אביי argues with a כל דכן that שחיטה needs a visible majority even more than טרפה does. That knocks down רבא's answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Isn't it all the more so? A טרפה is made by even a tiny bit of damage, and yet where it needs a majority, it needs a majority you can see. שחיטה is not kosher until there is a majority cut. Surely it also needs a majority you can see!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back against רבא's answer from the last step. He says the 'visible majority' rule should apply to שחיטה even more strongly than to טרפה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said that only טרפה needs a visible majority, while for שחיטה exactly half already counts as most. אביי turns this around. טרפה is the easier case, since even a tiny hole can make an animal טרפה, and still it demands a visible majority. So שחיטה, which requires a majority before it is kosher at all, should certainly demand a visible majority. That means half should not work for שחיטה.

keyTerms.meaning: All the more so; an argument from the easier case to the harder case (a קַל וָחוֹמֶר)
Any tiny amount
It becomes a טרפה
A majority that is clear to the eye
It becomes kosher (valid)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't get mixed up about which case is 'easier.' טרפה happens very easily, from even a tiny hole. A kosher שחיטה is hard to get, because a majority must be cut. That is why אביי says שחיטה should be at least as strict as טרפה.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him (to Rava):
But isn't it all the more so?
Just as with tereifa, where the animal becomes a tereifa from any tiny amount,
where we do require a majority,
we require a majority that is visible to the eyes;

phrases.aramaic: שְׁחִיטָה, דְּעַד דְּאִיכָּא רוּבָּא לָא מִיתַּכְשְׁרָא –
phrases.english: then slaughter, which is not valid until there is a majority,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן דְּבָעֵינַן רוֹב הַנִּרְאֶה לָעֵינַיִם?
phrases.english: isn't it all the more so that we require a majority visible to the eyes?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: וְלָא כָּל דְּכֵן הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבא's answer from step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's distinction that only טרפה needs a visible majority, while for שחיטה exactly half counts as most.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A כל דכן: if the easy-to-trigger טרפה needs a visible majority, then שחיטה, which needs a majority to be valid at all, surely does too.

steps.title: Everyone agrees half is not a majority, and the dispute was about קרבן פסח
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes course. For שחיטה, everyone holds that half is not like most. The dispute between רב and רב כהנא was said about קרבן פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, everyone agrees that half and half is not like a majority. When the dispute between רב and רב כהנא was stated, it was stated about פסח.
steps.whatsHappening: After אביי's attack, the גמרא gives up the idea that רב and רב כהנא argued about שחיטה. It moves their argument to a completely different topic, קרבן פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this, the גמרא thought one opinion held that half counts as most in שחיטה. Now no one holds that for שחיטה, so the earlier ברייתות are no longer a problem. The 'half is like most' opinion belongs to the laws of פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; this signals that the גמרא is dropping its earlier approach
Everyone agrees
Exactly half and half
The Pesach offering (קרבן פסח)

steps.whyThisMatters: This settles the שחיטה question. A סימן that is exactly half cut does not count as a majority.

phrases.english: Rather, according to everyone,
half and half is not like a majority,
and when the dispute of Rav and Rav Kahana was stated,
phrases.notes: This is their argument from earlier in the סוגיא about whether half counts as most.

phrases.english: it was stated regarding the Pesach offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא מֶחֱצָה עַל מֶחֱצָה אֵינוֹ כְּרוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to אביי's challenge by moving the whole dispute to a different topic.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigns the dispute to a different area of law (פסח instead of שחיטה).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב and רב כהנא argued about whether a half-cut סימן counts as most for שחיטה.
steps.terutzMaskana: For שחיטה, all agree half is not most. The argument concerns a nation that is half טמא at פסח time.

steps.title: The פסח case: half the nation pure, half impure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא spells out the dispute. If the Jewish people are half טהורים and half טמאים, רב says half counts as most and רב כהנא says it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the Jewish people were half טהורים and half טמאים, רב said half and half is like a majority, and רב כהנא said half and half is not like a majority.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now states the dispute between רב and רב כהנא as it really was said, about קרבן פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When most of the nation is טמא, everyone brings the פסח in טומאה at its normal time. For רב, half counts as 'most,' so the whole nation brings it in טומאה. For רב כהנא, half is not 'most,' so the טהורים bring it on time and the טמאים wait for פסח שני.

keyTerms.meaning: Ritually pure people
Ritually impure people
Like a majority

phrases.english: In a case where the Jewish people were
half pure and half impure,

phrases.aramaic: רַב אָמַר: מֶחֱצָה עַל מֶחֱצָה כְּרוֹב,
phrases.english: Rav said: half and half is like a majority,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב כָּהֲנָא אָמַר: מֶחֱצָה עַל מֶחֱצָה אֵינוֹ כְּרוֹב.
phrases.english: and Rav Kahana said: half and half is not like a majority.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲרֵי שֶׁהָיוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל מֶחֱצָה טְהוֹרִים וּמֶחֱצָה טְמֵאִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the פסח dispute that step 6 pointed to.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: a nation that is half טמא counts as a majority טמא. רב כהנא: it does not.

steps.title: What is רב's reason in the Pesach case?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רב treats half as most in the case of פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: And there, what is רב's reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source behind רב's opinion. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We just learned that everyone agrees half is not most in שחיטה. So why should half be different for פסח? The גמרא wants a reason that applies only to פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
There (here it means in the case of פסח)

phrases.english: And there, what is Rav's reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind רב's opinion from step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רב counts half as a majority for פסח, when half is not a majority for שחיטה.

steps.title: An individual is pushed off, but a community is not
steps.stepSummary: רב learns from the פסוק 'איש איש' that an individual who is טמא is pushed off to פסח שני, but a ציבור is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'Any man who shall be impure by reason of a corpse.' An individual is pushed off, but a community is not pushed off.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק. The Torah sends only an individual טמא to פסח שני, not a whole community.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule of פסח שני is written about an 'איש,' one person. Half of the Jewish people is not a scattered group of individuals. It is a ציבור. So for רב, a ציבור that is טמא does not get pushed off, even if it is only half the nation. This reason belongs only to פסח, which is why it does not affect שחיטה.

keyTerms.meaning: Impure from contact with a dead body
Is pushed off (to פֶּסַח שֵׁנִי)
The community as a whole
The makeup פסח, one month later

steps.whatToRemember: For שחיטה, everyone agrees that half is not a majority. רב's 'half is like most' applies only to פסח, because half the nation counts as a ציבור, and a ציבור is not pushed off to פסח שני.

phrases.aramaic: דִּכְתִיב ״אִישׁ אִישׁ כִּי יִהְיֶה טָמֵא לָנֶפֶשׁ״,
phrases.english: As it is written: "Any man who shall be impure by reason of a corpse,"
an individual is pushed off (to the second Pesach),
but a community is not pushed off.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב אִישׁ אִישׁ כִּי יִהְיֶה טָמֵא לָנֶפֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: From 'איש': only individuals are pushed off to פסח שני. Half the nation is a ציבור, so it is not pushed off.

steps.title: Why does the משנה repeat the rule of most of one סימן?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line about cutting most of one סימן in a bird and asks why it is needed, since the משנה already taught that most of a סימן is like all of it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: most of one סימן in a bird is enough. But we already learned that once: most of one סימן is like all of it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new section. It quotes a line from the משנה and points out that the משנה seems to say the same thing twice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A משנה does not waste words. Earlier it said that cutting most of a סימן counts like cutting the whole thing. So the later line about cutting most of one סימן in a bird looks like an extra repeat, and the גמרא wants to know what it adds.

keyTerms.meaning: Most, the majority
One of the two pipes cut in שחיטה: the windpipe or the food pipe
We already learned this once (the משנה is repeating itself)
Most of something counts like all of it

steps.confusionAlert: This is a new topic. It is not connected to the פסח discussion of רב and רב כהנא in the last steps. The גמרא has gone back to explain the words of the משנה.

phrases.english: The majority of one [סימן] in a bird [is valid]
We already learned this one time:
The majority of one is like all of it!
phrases.notes: This is an earlier line in the same משנה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section. The גמרא goes back to the משנה's words after the רב and רב כהנא discussion.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rule was already stated earlier in the משנה ('רובו של אחד כמוהו'), so the second line looks like a needless repeat.

steps.title: A memory aid for the coming discussion
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a set of letters to help remember the names of the sages who speak in the coming discussion.
steps.simpleTranslation: (The memory aid: ה, כ, ש, פ, ש, ח.)
steps.whatsHappening: This is not an argument. The גמרא is setting up the next part of the discussion by giving a memory aid for the names of the sages who will speak.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each letter hints at a sage whose words come next, like ה for רב הושעיא. It helped people who learned by heart keep the order straight. It does not change the law.

keyTerms.meaning: Here it means a memory aid, a sign to help remember the order

phrases.english: (A memory aid: ה, כ, ש, פ, ש, ח.)
phrases.notes: Each letter hints at a sage in the coming discussion, like ה for רב הושעיא. Here סימן means 'memory aid,' not a pipe of the throat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A pause in the argument that lists the sages who will answer the question from step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling. This is only a memory aid for the names of the sages.

steps.title: רב הושעיא: one line is about חולין, one is about קדשים
steps.stepSummary: רב הושעיא answers that the two lines are not a repeat. One teaches the rule for חולין and the other teaches it for קדשים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הושעיא said: One line is about חולין, and one line is about קדשים.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הושעיא answers the question from step 10. He says each line teaches about a different kind of animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule that most of a סימן counts like all of it is the same in both lines. What changes is the case: regular food animals (חולין) or animals brought as offerings (קדשים). So the משנה is not repeating itself.

keyTerms.meaning: Regular, non-holy animals slaughtered for food
Holy animals brought as offerings

phrases.english: Rav Hoshaya said:
One is about non-holy animals, and one is about holy offerings,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the redundancy question from step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: each line of the משנה teaches about a different kind of animal.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both lines seem to say the same thing.
steps.terutzMaskana: One line teaches the rule for חולין and the other teaches it for קדשים.

steps.title: Why we need the line for קדשים
steps.stepSummary: If the משנה had taught only חולין, we might think that קדשים need the whole סימן cut, because there the blood is needed for the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: And both are needed. If the משנה had only taught חולין, we would say: there most is enough, because he does not need the blood. But in קדשים, where he does need the blood, we would say most is not enough until he cuts all of it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins to show why both lines are needed. Here it explains what we would have gotten wrong if the משנה taught only חולין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With קדשים, the blood is collected and put on the מזבח, so it matters how well the blood comes out. Because of that, we might have thought a full cut is needed there. The line about קדשים teaches that most is enough even there.

keyTerms.meaning: And it is needed (both cases have to be taught)
It is enough for him
He needs the blood (for the מזבח)
I would say (what we would have mistakenly thought)

phrases.english: And it is necessary [to teach both],
for if it had taught us only non-holy animals –
it is there that a majority is enough,
because he does not need the blood,
but holy offerings, where he needs the blood –
I would say a majority is not enough for him
until the whole [סימן] is cut.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the 'both are needed' reasoning that supports רב הושעיא's answer in step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: showing that each case needs to be taught on its own.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With only חולין taught, we might think קדשים need the whole סימן cut, because the blood is needed.
steps.terutzMaskana: The line for קדשים teaches that most is enough even there.

steps.title: Why we need the line for חולין
steps.stepSummary: If the משנה had taught only קדשים, we might think חולין need only half, since the blood is not needed. So the משנה teaches both.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the משנה had only taught קדשים, we would say most is needed there because he needs the blood. But in חולין, where he does not need the blood, we would say half is enough. So the משנה teaches us both.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes showing why both lines are needed. It explains what we would have gotten wrong if the משנה taught only קדשים, and then concludes that the משנה teaches both.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This mistake goes the other way. We might think the need for blood is the only reason קדשים need most of the סימן cut, so חולין could get by with half. The line about חולין teaches that חולין also need most, not just half.

keyTerms.meaning: Half
It teaches us (that this mistake is wrong)

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה says 'most of a סימן is like all of it' twice: once for חולין and once for קדשים. Each line blocks a different mistake. For קדשים, we might have needed the whole סימן. For חולין, we might have thought half is enough. The answer for both is that most is needed, and most is enough.
steps.whyThisMatters: It sets the rule for both kinds of animals: most of the סימן is needed and most is enough, whether the blood is used or not.

phrases.english: And if it had taught us only holy offerings,
[I would say a majority is needed there] because he needs the blood,
phrases.notes: The גמרא leaves out the first half of the thought. It means that only for an offering would most of the סימן be required.

phrases.english: but non-holy animals, where he does not need the blood –
I would say half is enough for him,
[so] it teaches us [that this is not so].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the 'both are needed' reasoning begun in step 13 with the other side, and closes the answer to step 10.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה is not repeating itself. One line is for קדשים and one is for חולין, and in both cases most of the סימן is needed and is enough.

steps.title: Which line is about חולין and which is about קדשים?
steps.stepSummary: Since one line of the משנה teaches חולין and the other teaches קדשים, the גמרא asks which line teaches which.
steps.simpleTranslation: Which one is about חולין, and which one is about קדשים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts רב הושעיא's answer and now asks a follow-up question. Which line of the משנה is about חולין, and which is about קדשים? This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הושעיא said the two lines are not a repeat, because one is for חולין and one is for קדשים. He did not say which line is which. The גמרא now wants that detail filled in.

keyTerms.meaning: Ordinary food that is not holy, like a regular chicken or cow
Holy offerings brought in the בית המקדש
The first part of a משנה
The later part of a משנה

phrases.english: Which one is about non-holy animals,
and which one is about holy offerings?
phrases.notes: "Which one" means which of the two lines in the משנה about cutting most of a סימן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follow-up question on רב הושעיא's answer
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which line of the משנה refers to חולין and which refers to קדשים

steps.title: רב כהנא: the first line is חולין and the later line is קדשים
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא says it makes sense that the רישא is about חולין and the סיפא is about קדשים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: It makes sense that the first line is about חולין and the later line is about קדשים.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא answers the question. He says the first line is about חולין and the later line is about קדשים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He calls this what "makes sense". That means his answer comes from reasoning about the משנה's wording, not from a teaching he received. The גמרא will ask for his reason in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense; it is reasonable

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said:
It makes sense that the first line is about non-holy animals
and the later line is about holy offerings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 15
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The רישא is about חולין and the סיפא is about קדשים

steps.title: The proof: the first line says "one who slaughters"
steps.stepSummary: The רישא says "השוחט". A bird brought as קדשים is not slaughtered but done by מליקה, so the רישא must be about חולין.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know this? Because the first line says "one who slaughters." If you thought the first line was about קדשים, it should have said "one who pinches."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how רב כהנא knows this, and then gives his proof from one word in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A bird offering is not killed with a knife. The כהן does מליקה, cutting the neck with his fingernail. The רישא opens with a bird and uses the word "השוחט", so it must be talking about an ordinary bird, which is חולין.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know this?
How a bird offering is killed: the כהן cuts the back of its neck with his fingernail
If you thought that; it introduces an idea in order to reject it
He should have said

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think holy birds are slaughtered with a knife like animals. Holy birds get מליקה, and only holy animals get שחיטה. The whole proof depends on this difference.

phrases.english: From where do we know this?
From the fact that it teaches "one who slaughters,"
and if you thought the first line is about holy offerings,
it should have said "one who pinches."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for רב כהנא's claim
steps.raayaSupportSource: The word "השוחט" in the רישא, since a holy bird gets מליקה and not שחיטה

steps.title: But the later line also says "his slaughter is valid"
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if the סיפא is about קדשים, why does it say "שחיטתו כשרה"? It should say "מליקתו כשרה".
steps.simpleTranslation: But what then, is the later line about קדשים? It says "his slaughter is valid"! It should have said "his pinching is valid"!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns רב כהנא's own proof against him. The later line also uses a word about slaughtering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the word "slaughter" proves the רישא is not about קדשים, the same word should prove that about the סיפא too. That would leave neither line about holy birds. So רב כהנא's proof looks like it breaks.

keyTerms.meaning: But what then? It introduces a challenge to the suggestion just made
His slaughter is valid

phrases.english: But what then, is the later line about holy offerings?
It says "his slaughter is valid"?
It should have said "his pinching is valid"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב כהנא's proof using the same kind of reasoning
steps.kashyaTarget: רב כהנא's claim that the סיפא is about קדשים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The סיפא also uses the word "slaughter". By רב כהנא's own logic, it cannot be about holy birds either.

steps.title: The later line ends with an animal, so "slaughter" fits
steps.stepSummary: The סיפא ends with an animal, and holy animals do get שחיטה. So the משנה used "שחיטתו כשרה" for both cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is not difficult. Since it ended with an animal, it also taught "his slaughter is valid."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The later line can still use the word "slaughter", because it ends by talking about an animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The סיפא lists the bird first and the animal last. Holy animals really are slaughtered with a knife. So "שחיטתו כשרה" fits the animal, and the משנה used one word to cover both cases.

keyTerms.meaning: That is not difficult
Since; the משנה chose its wording because of the nearby case

phrases.english: That is not difficult,
since it ended with an animal
it also taught "his slaughter is valid."

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא לָא קַשְׁיָא, אַיְּידֵי דְּסָלֵיק מִבְּהֵמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 18
steps.terutzResolutionType: The wording follows the last case mentioned
steps.terutzHavaAmina: "Slaughter" in the סיפא shows it cannot be about קדשים
steps.terutzMaskana: The word fits the animal at the end of the סיפא, and the משנה used it for the bird too

steps.title: But the first line opens with a bird, so it has no excuse
steps.stepSummary: The רישא begins with a bird. If it were about קדשים, it should have said "המולק", so the original proof still stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the first line, since it is talking about a bird, if you thought it was about קדשים, it should have said "one who pinches"!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the same excuse does not work for the first line. This brings back רב כהנא's proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the רישא, the word "השוחט" comes right before the bird case ("one in a bird"). The animal case does not come first, so nothing else could explain the word. So the רישא must be about חולין.

keyTerms.meaning: Since; after all
Is standing on; is dealing with

steps.whatToRemember: רב כהנא: the רישא is about חולין, because it opens with a bird and says "השוחט". The סיפא can be about קדשים, because its "שחיטתו כשרה" fits the animal it ends with.

phrases.english: But the first line,
since it is dealing with a bird,
if you thought it is about holy offerings,
it should have said "one who pinches"!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא רֵישָׁא, מִכְּדֵי עַל עוֹף קָאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the answer in step 19 does not weaken the proof for the רישא
steps.raayaSupportSource: The רישא opens with a bird and uses "השוחט", which cannot fit a holy bird

steps.title: רב שימי בר אשי: a different proof from "one in a bird"
steps.stepSummary: רב שימי בר אשי proves the רישא is about חולין in another way. The רישא says one סימן is enough for a bird, but an עולת העוף needs two סימנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שימי בר אשי said: The first line is about חולין, and we know it from here. It teaches "one in a bird." If you thought it was about קדשים, there is the עולת העוף, which needs two סימנים!
steps.whatsHappening: רב שימי בר אשי gives a different proof that the first line is about חולין. His proof comes from the law, not from the choice of word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רישא says cutting one סימן in a bird is enough. A holy bird brought as an עולה must have both סימנים cut. So a line that says one סימן is enough cannot be about קדשים.

keyTerms.meaning: A bird brought as a burnt offering
Both signs: the windpipe and the food pipe
From here

steps.whatToRemember: There are two proofs that the רישא is about חולין. רב כהנא's proof is the word "השוחט". רב שימי בר אשי's proof is that an עולת העוף needs two סימנים, but the רישא allows one.

phrases.english: Rav Shimi bar Ashi said:
The first line is about non-holy animals, from here:
for it teaches "one in a bird,"
and if you thought it is about holy offerings,
there is the bird burnt offering
which needs two signs!

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב שִׁימִי בַּר אָשֵׁי אָמַר: רֵישָׁא בְּחוּלִּין מֵהָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Agrees with רב כהנא's conclusion but gives a different proof
steps.raayaSupportSource: An עולת העוף needs two סימנים, so a rule allowing one סימן cannot be about קדשים

steps.title: The bird burnt offering problem hits the latter clause too
steps.stepSummary: If the סיפא is about קדשים, how can it say the majority of one סימן is enough for a bird, when an עולת העוף needs two?
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what are you saying, that the סיפא is about קדשים? It says the majority of one סימן works for a bird. But an עולת העוף needs two סימנים!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the same question from Step 21 against the idea that the סיפא is about קדשים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 21 used עולת העוף to show the רישא cannot be about קדשים. But the סיפא also says 'רוב אחד בעוף', so the same problem seems to hit it. If the סיפא were about קדשים, it would be wrong for an עולת העוף.

keyTerms.meaning: The latter clause of the משנה
Holy offerings brought in the בית המקדש
A bird brought as a burnt offering, done by מליקה
The windpipe and the foodpipe, which must be cut in slaughter

phrases.english: Rather, what? The latter clause is about sacred offerings?
The majority of one [סימן] in a bird [is enough]?
But there is the bird burnt offering
which requires two סימנים!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the argument of Step 21 and applies it to the סיפא
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the סיפא is about קדשים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The סיפא says one סימן is enough for a bird, but an עולת העוף needs two, so the סיפא cannot be about קדשים either

steps.title: 'Majority of one' means the majority of each one
steps.stepSummary: 'רוב אחד' in the סיפא means the majority of each of the two סימנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'the majority of one' mean? The majority of each and every one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by reading 'רוב אחד' in a new way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'רוב אחד' does not mean cutting the majority of only one סימן. It means cutting the majority of each סימן. With this reading, the סיפא fits an עולת העוף, which needs both סימנים.

keyTerms.meaning: Majority, more than half
The majority of each and every one

phrases.english: What does 'the majority of one' mean?
The majority of each and every one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 22
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'רוב אחד' means the majority of just one סימן
steps.terutzMaskana: 'רוב אחד' means the majority of each סימן, so it works for an עולת העוף

steps.title: Then the משנה should have said 'majority of two'
steps.stepSummary: If both סימנים are meant, the משנה should simply have said 'רוב שנים'.
steps.simpleTranslation: By right, the משנה should have taught 'the majority of two'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer of Step 23.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the תנא meant the majority of both סימנים, the clear way to say it is 'רוב שנים', as he says for an animal. Saying 'רוב אחד' looks like the wrong way to say it.

keyTerms.meaning: By right, it would make sense
He should have taught

phrases.english: And by right
he should have taught 'the majority of two'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the wording implied by the answer in Step 23
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If two סימנים are meant, 'רוב שנים' would be the natural wording

steps.title: The bird sin offering needs only one סימן
steps.stepSummary: The תנא could not say 'two' as a set rule, because a חטאת העוף needs only one סימן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since there is the חטאת, which is fine with one סימן, the rule is not clear-cut, so the תנא could not say 'two'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the משנה used the word 'one'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Among bird offerings, an עולה needs two סימנים but a חטאת needs only one. Writing 'שנים' would have been wrong for the חטאת. So the תנא wrote 'רוב אחד', which works both ways: one סימן for a חטאת, and each one for an עולה.

keyTerms.meaning: Sin offering; here, a bird sin offering
It is enough for it
It is not a fixed, across-the-board rule for him

steps.whatToRemember: According to this reading, the סיפא can be about קדשים: 'רוב אחד' covers both the עולת העוף (each סימן) and the חטאת העוף (one סימן).

phrases.english: Since there is the [bird] sin offering
for which one סימן is enough
because of that, it is not clear-cut for him.
phrases.notes: He means the תנא could not write 'two' as one rule for all birds, since the חטאת needs only one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 24
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the chosen wording by pointing to a case where 'two' would be wrong
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The תנא should have written 'רוב שנים'
steps.terutzMaskana: 'רוב אחד' was chosen because it fits both the חטאת and the עולה of birds

steps.title: רב פפא proves the first clause is about non-sacred birds
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה requires cutting the ורידין and the רבנן disagree. For קדשים, everyone would want the blood, so the רישא must be about חולין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: We see the רישא is about חולין from this. רבי יהודה says the slaughter is not valid until he cuts the veins, and the רבנן disagree. That works if it is about חולין. But if it is about קדשים, why would the רבנן disagree? The one slaughtering needs the blood!
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא brings a new proof that the רישא is about חולין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With קדשים, the blood must be put on the מזבח, and cutting the ורידין makes the blood flow out. So for קדשים, the רבנן would have no reason to argue with רבי יהודה. Since they do argue, the case must be חולין.

keyTerms.meaning: The first clause of the משנה
Ordinary, non-holy food
The neck veins, the main blood vessels
It is fine if you say..., but...
He needs the blood

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
[We know] the first clause is about non-sacred [birds] from here,
as it teaches: Rabbi Yehuda says:
[It is not valid] until he cuts the veins,
and the Rabbis disagree with him.
It is fine if you say it is about non-sacred,
but if you say it is about sacred offerings,
why do the Rabbis disagree with him?
He himself needs the blood!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third proof that the רישא is about חולין, after Steps 17 and 21
steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר: רֵישָׁא בְּחוּלִּין מֵהָכָא
steps.raayaObject: That the רישא is about חולין
steps.raayaSupportSource: The argument in the משנה between רבי יהודה and the רבנן about cutting the ורידין

steps.title: רב אשי's proof begins: two heads at once only after the fact
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says one who slaughters two heads at once has a valid slaughter. This implies it is valid after the fact but not allowed from the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: We see the סיפא is about קדשים from this. It teaches: One who slaughters two heads at once, his slaughter is valid. 'One who slaughters' means after the fact, yes; from the start, no.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי starts a proof that the סיפא is about קדשים, first pulling a point out of the משנה's wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'השוחט' describes something already done, so 'valid' means valid only after the fact. That shows there is a rule against doing it from the start. The next step will show this rule fits קדשים.

keyTerms.meaning: From here, from this source
Two heads at the same time
After the fact, once it was already done
From the start, as the proper way to act

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
[We know] the latter clause is about sacred offerings from here,
as it teaches: One who slaughters two heads at once,
his slaughter is valid.
'One who slaughters': after the fact, yes,
from the start, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from proving the רישא is חולין to proving the סיפא is קדשים
steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: סֵיפָא בְּקָדָשִׁים מֵהָכָא
steps.raayaObject: That the סיפא is about קדשים
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about slaughtering two heads at once, read as valid only after the fact

steps.title: For offerings there is a verse against slaughtering two at once
steps.stepSummary: If the case is קדשים, the rule against slaughtering two at once from the start makes sense because of רב יוסף's teaching on 'תזבחהו'.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works if you say it is about קדשים: that is why it is not allowed from the start. רב יוסף taught: 'תזבח' teaches that two people should not slaughter one offering. 'תזבחהו' teaches that one person should not slaughter two offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי shows why the 'not from the start' rule fits קדשים. This sets up the next move, where the גמרא will point out that for חולין there would be no such reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף learns from the פסוק that one person should not slaughter two offerings at once. That gives a clear reason for the לכתחלה rule if the case is קדשים. The other side of the proof, that חולין has no such reason, comes right after this.

keyTerms.meaning: That is why, that explains
An offering that is slaughtered
You shall slaughter
You shall slaughter it

phrases.english: It is fine if you say it is about sacred offerings:
that is why it is not allowed from the start,
because of what Rav Yosef taught:
'You shall slaughter':
phrases.notes: ויקרא 19:5. The word there is 'תזבחהו', and he reads it in two parts, 'תזבח' and 'הו' (it).

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא שְׁנַיִם שׁוֹחֲטִים זֶבַח אֶחָד,
phrases.english: that two people should not slaughter one offering;
'You shall slaughter it':

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא אֶחָד שׁוֹחֵט שְׁנֵי זְבָחִים.
phrases.english: that one person should not slaughter two offerings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason behind the inference of Step 27 if the case is קדשים
steps.raayaObject: That the סיפא is about קדשים
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב יוסף's teaching from 'תזבחהו' that one person should not slaughter two offerings

steps.title: רב כהנא explains the spelling, and רב אשי finishes his proof
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא explains רב יוסף's first teaching: the word is spelled 'תזבחהו', in the singular, so two people may not slaughter one offering. רב אשי then finishes his proof. If the משנה were about חולין, slaughtering two at once would be allowed even from the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב כהנא said: The word is written "תזבחהו" (singular). [רב אשי continues:] But if you say the case is about חולין, it should be allowed even from the start.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds רב כהנא's explanation of how רב יוסף learns that two people may not slaughter one offering. Then רב אשי finishes his proof: for חולין there would be no reason to forbid slaughtering two at once from the start.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word is read aloud as plural ('תִּזְבָּחֻהוּ'), which might suggest that two people may slaughter together. But it is spelled singular, and that spelling teaches that two may not slaughter one offering. רב אשי's point is that these limits from the פסוק apply only to a קרבן. Ordinary חולין have no such limit, so 'only after the fact' fits only קדשים.

keyTerms.meaning: "You shall slaughter it": a word in the פסוק about קרבנות whose written spelling is singular
"It is written": pointing to how the word is spelled, not how it is read aloud
Even from the start as well

steps.whyThisMatters: This finishes the proof that the סיפא of the משנה is about קדשים, which sets up ריש לקיש's agreement in the next step.

phrases.english: And Rav Kahana said:
"Tizbachehu" (singular) is written,
but if you say it is about non-holy animals,
it should be allowed even from the start.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds רב כהנא's note on the spelling in רב יוסף's teaching from Step 28, then completes רב אשי's proof by showing that the restriction would not apply to חולין.
steps.raayaObject: That the סיפא of the משנה ("two heads at once") deals with קדשים
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב יוסף's teaching from תזבחהו applies only to קרבנות. For חולין there is no reason to forbid slaughtering two heads at once even from the start.

steps.title: ריש לקיש Also Splits the משנה Between Ordinary and Holy Animals
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings support. ריש לקיש also holds that the first part of the משנה is about חולין and the last part is about קדשים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And ריש לקיש also holds: the first part is about חולין, and the last part is about קדשים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that its conclusion is shared by ריש לקיש. This line sets up the quote of ריש לקיש that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word "also" (וְאַף) tells us this is support for the view just proven, not a new idea. The proof that ריש לקיש really holds this comes in the next steps, from his own words.

keyTerms.meaning: "And also": bringing another sage who holds the same view
The first part of the משנה
The last part of the משנה
Holy animals or birds set aside for קרבנות

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ סָבַר:
phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish also holds:
the first part is about non-holy animals, and the last part is about holy ones,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַף רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ סָבַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a supporting sage to the conclusion reached in Steps 26 to 29.
steps.raayaObject: The split reading: רישא about חולין, סיפא about קדשים
steps.raayaSupportSource: ריש לקיש's own explanation, quoted next

steps.title: Why Does the משנה Repeat the Majority Rule?
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש asks why the משנה says "most of one סימן in a bird and most of two in an animal" when it already taught that most of a סימן counts like the whole.
steps.simpleTranslation: For ריש לקיש said: Since we already learned "most of one is like all of it," why did we also learn "most of one in a bird and most of two in an animal"?
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש points out that the משנה seems to say the same rule twice. He asks what the second statement adds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה already taught that cutting most of a סימן counts as cutting all of it. Saying again that most of one סימן in a bird, or most of two in an animal, is valid looks unnecessary. The question is a setup: his answer will show that the second statement is about קדשים.

keyTerms.meaning: "Since we already learned": pointing out that a rule was already taught
Most of one סימן counts like the whole סימן
The windpipe and the food pipe, which must be cut in שחיטה

phrases.english: For Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:
Since we learned "the majority of one is like it,"
phrases.notes: He means most of one סימן counts like the whole סימן. That is the opening line of our משנה.

phrases.english: why did we learn "the majority of one in a bird
and the majority of two in an animal"?

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵאַחַר שֶׁשָּׁנִינוּ ״רוּבּוֹ שֶׁל אֶחָד כָּמוֹהוּ״, לָמָּה שָׁנִינוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes ריש לקיש to back up the claim in Step 30.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the seemingly repeated clause "most of one in a bird and most of two in an animal" comes to teach

steps.title: The Repetition Teaches About the Daily Offering on יום כיפור
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש answers that the repetition is for the תמיד on יום כיפור. There, the כהן גדול cut most of the סימנים and another כהן finished. The משנה teaches that the slaughter is valid even if nobody finished.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because we learned: They brought him the תמיד, he cut most of it, and another finished the slaughter for him. I might think that if the other did not finish, it would be invalid. That is why we learned: most of one in a bird and most of two in an animal.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש explains that the second statement is needed for a case of קדשים: the קרבן תמיד that the כהן גדול slaughters on יום כיפור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On יום כיפור the כהן גדול cuts most of the סימנים and another כהן finishes. Seeing that, we might think finishing is required for a קרבן. The סיפא teaches that cutting most is enough even for קדשים, so finishing is not required. This proves ריש לקיש reads the סיפא as being about קדשים.

keyTerms.meaning: The daily communal קרבן offered morning and afternoon
"He cut it": cutting most of the way through the סימנים
Finished, completed the cut
"I might have thought": introducing a wrong idea the text comes to reject

steps.whatToRemember: ריש לקיש: the סיפא ("most of one in a bird, most of two in an animal") is needed for קדשים. It teaches that the תמיד is valid even if the second כהן never finished the cut.
steps.confusionAlert: The second כהן finishing the cut is not what makes the שחיטה valid. It was already valid once most of the סימנים were cut. The finishing is extra.

phrases.english: Because we learned:
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in יומא about the יום כיפור service.

phrases.english: They brought him the daily offering,
phrases.notes: "Him" is the כהן גדול on יום כיפור.

phrases.english: he cut it most of the way, and another finished its slaughter for him,
I might think that if he did not finish, it would be invalid?

phrases.english: the majority of one in a bird and the majority of two in an animal.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְפִי שֶׁשָּׁנִינוּ: הֵבִיאוּ לוֹ אֶת הַתָּמִיד

steps.title: Quoting ריש לקיש's Line in Order to Examine It
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes one line from ריש לקיש's answer, "I might think that if he did not finish it would be invalid," so it can analyze it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: I might think that if he did not finish, it would be invalid?

steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase "אמר מר" signals that the גמרא is going back to a statement just quoted in order to look at it closely. No challenge is stated yet. The question about this line comes on the next amud.
